title: Biot-Savart Law
notes: The Biot–Savart law gives the magnetic field due to a tiny current element: dB = (μ0 / 4π) I dl sinθ / r^2. The direction is perpendicular to the element and to the line from the element to the point.
A long straight wire is the integral of that law, and the result is B = μ0 I /(2π r). The field circles the wire, given by the right-hand grip.
At the centre of a single circular loop the result is B = μ0 I /(2 R), along the axis. A coil of N turns multiplies this by N if the turns are together.
On the axis of a loop, off centre, the field is along the axis and weaker. The perpendicular components from opposite elements cancel.
μ0 / 4π is 10^−7, and μ0 is 4π × 10^−7. Using the wrong one is the usual numerical slip.
The law is the magnetic analogue of Coulomb's law for a current element. It is the starting point. Ampere's law is the shortcut when symmetry is high.
confusion: ❌ 'Biot-Savart law gives the total magnetic field directly.' ✅ It gives the *contribution* dB from a tiny element dl; the total field requires integration over the entire conductor.
❌ 'The magnetic field is parallel to the current element.' ✅ dB is *perpendicular* to both dl and r̂ (given by the cross product dl × r̂).
❌ 'Biot-Savart law applies to moving charges but not currents.' ✅ A current is just moving charges; the law applies to *both* — for a charge: dB = (μ₀/4π)·(qv×r̂)/r².
The straight-wire field is not μ0 I /(2R). That is the loop centre.
The field circles a straight wire. It is not radial.
sinθ is zero for a point on the line of the element.
